---
title: "fleet"
subtitle: "Overview and sync of Git repositories across hosting providers."
---

Repositories accumulate across hosting providers, and local clones drift away from them.
Some remotes are never cloned.
Some clones are abandoned, renamed, or forgotten.
Forks fall behind their upstream.

`fleet` gives one view of that landscape and safe, scriptable actions to close the gap.

GitHub is the only supported provider for now.

::: {.callout-important}

## Status

Early development.

The command surface is not yet implemented; the repository currently contains the project scaffold only.
This site documents commands as they land, never before.

:::

## Design goals

- Every capability is a command-line command first, so a person, a script, or an agent can reach any outcome the interactive interface offers.
- Read-only by default: comparison never mutates a working tree, and every mutating action is explicit and opt-in.
- Nothing destructive happens implicitly: no force-push, no rebase, and no discarding of local changes.
- Durable state lives in plain text that can be read, edited, and version-controlled by hand.

## Requirements

- Rust 1.85 or later, for building from source.
- A `git` binary on `PATH`, which `fleet` shells out to so that existing SSH agents and credential helpers keep working.

## Documentation

- [Design note](design.qmd) covers the provider abstraction and the comparison and sync state machine.

Installation, configuration, and per-command reference pages are added as the corresponding features are implemented.
